neighbours.label: the craft of painting pictures: a painter at work and the tools of the easel (canvas, palette, oil paint, brushes); a house painter or decorator, and other visual arts (sculpture, photography) stay low
fire: The painter squeezed cobalt blue onto her palette.
He set the half-finished canvas on the easel by the window.
Every morning the old painter worked on a portrait of his wife.
She thinned the oil paint with turpentine before the next layer.
Art students copy the masters' canvases in the museum.
The landscape painter carried a folding easel up the hill.
Layers of varnish protect the paint on old canvases.
A young painter rented a cold attic in Montmartre.
quiet: The house painter rolled a second coat onto the ceiling.
He set the half-finished vase on the shelf by the window.
Every morning the old sculptor worked on a bust of his wife.
She thinned the soup with stock before the next serving.
Art students sketch the statues in the museum.
The landscape photographer carried a folding tripod up the hill.
Layers of varnish protect the floorboards in old houses.
A young poet rented a cold attic in Montmartre.
